item.title: Shiramizu Amidado: A Heian-Era National Treasure Temple — Guide
item.description: Shiramizu Amidado, built in 1160 by the widow of a regional lord to pray for her late husband’s soul, is a National Treasure and one of only a handful of surviving Heian-period Pure Land Buddhist temple gardens in Japan. The hall sits on an island in a lotus pond, meant to evoke the Buddhist paradise of the Pure Land, with the wooden structure and its seated Amida Buddha reflected serenely in the water — a rare, intact glimpse of 12th-century religious architecture.
